answer: A garden of agents stays healthy when trust is earned slowly and fades without upkeep: each newcomer starts with almost no influence and gains weight only by completing verified work over weeks, while idle identities steadily lose standing. A beacon of activity records this history, so a sudden swarm of fresh clones cannot vote, price, or claim rewards at once. Attackers would need to run every fake identity through months of useful work to match one established agent, turning a cheap Sybil flood into a costly, slow farm, with no safe haven for identities that appear overnight and vanish.
